exact_statement: For any Boolean pair on independent uniform bits, before a fresh selector is revealed, let delta be the physical mismatch probability and let eligibility be absorbing under data restrictions. At marked private queries suppose expected eligible-child mismatch mass is at most (1-gamma) times the parent mismatch, 0<gamma<=1. The single mark M=(4/gamma)delta*1_eligible pays sum_marked w[B_i(mux)-B_i(private core)/4]+E M_leaf<=M_root. For every even k>=2,r>=1, let G=1-2*1{s=0,x=0},H=(-1)^(sum paired s-coordinate products),A=1{r controls zero}, Gp=1+A(G-1),Hp=1+A(H-1),W=mux_z(Gp,Hp). At every restriction before z is revealed, eligibility means active gates, a surviving nonconstant point-defect base G and nonconstant base H. Every eligible G-private exposure contracts the weighted eligible mismatch mass by at least1/3; the2/3 surviving fraction is attained at k=2 private x for every r. Set K=12delta*1_eligible+10delta*1_z_unqueried, and K=0 after z revelation. Every finite adaptive fresh-coordinate stopping tree, including arbitrary early selector revelation and arbitrary interleaving, satisfies B_tree(W)+E K_leaf<=10P_data+K_root, K_root=22Inf_z(W). Coordinate-wise influence conservation gives P_data=I_data(root)-E I_data(leaf),P_z=Inf_z(root)-E Inf_z(leaf). The exact entropy law is H(W)=B_tree+JS_tree+E H(actual leaf),JS_tree<=2(P_data+P_z)/ln2; unqueried-selector leaf entropy is half both residual core entropies plus the exact paired Fourier potential. Complete constant-leaf trees have B_tree,Q_tree<=22I(W),H(W)<25I(W). The existing class entropy bound H(W)<8I(W) remains stronger; the new result is repeated-exposure ownership with retained terminal banks. No released-child hypothesis is proved for arbitrary cores whose two children remain eligible.
